zones/kitchen-worktop.description: Wie viele Lumen unter Oberschränken, welche Kelvin- und CRI-Werte, drei Netz-LED-Leisten im Vergleich (lm/m). Ziel: 500 Lux auf der Arbeitsplatte.
zones/kitchen-worktop.lead: Das Deckenlicht erhellt die Küche, aber Sie kochen mit dem Rücken zur Lampe — Ihr Körper wirft Schatten auf die Platte. Die Lösung: Licht unter den Hängeschränken, zwischen Ihnen und der Arbeitsfläche.
zones/kitchen-worktop.body:
Drei Zahlen merken

  • 500 lux auf der Arbeitsplatte zum Schneiden und Lesen von Rezepten — our “detailed task” benchmark in Lux pro Raum.
  • 420 lm per metre Mindestwert: for a 3.0 × 0.6 m worktop, 500 lx × 1.8 m² × factor 1.4 (close source) ≈ 1,260 lm, i.e. 420 lm/m of cabinet run.
  • 4000 K and CRI (Farbwiedergabeindex (CRI)) ≥ 80 (90 if you can) to judge food without a colour cast — see Farbtemperatur and CRI.

Lumen pro Meter = angegebener Lichtstrom ÷ length (Herstellerangaben, geprüft 23.10.2026). Alle Leisten liegen über 420 lm/m; entscheidend sind Farbe, Montage und Länge.

Keine Steckdose unter den Schränken?

A rechargeable bar (e.g. OUILA 60 cm on the French site) suits backup use; if the maker does not publish lumens, do not rely on it as the main worktop light.

Leiste oder LED-Streifen?

A bar screws in and plugs in — about 15 minutes. Strip in an aluminium profile gives a continuous line but needs a sized 24 V driver. See under-cabinet LED strip.

Montage

  • As far forward on the wall unit as possible so light hits the board, not only the splashback.
  • One bar per cabinet run, leaving 2–3 cm at each end for end caps.
  • Nothing over the sink without the right IP rating.

guides/smart-bulb-gift-ideas.body:
Three questions before buying

  1. Welcher Sockel? E27 in most pendants, E14 for small shades, GU10 for spot fittings. See bulb bases.
  2. Welche Funkverbindung? Wi-Fi works without a hub but needs the router’s 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi band (many IoT devices do not join 5 GHz). Zigbee needs a hub (Hue Bridge, some smart speakers) but scales better with many bulbs. Philips Hue also works over Bluetooth for up to about ten bulbs in one room.
  3. Nur Weiß oder Farbe? Tunable white suits daily use; colour is mainly for mood and TV sync.

Symptom: Status offline in WiZ V2.

Ursachen: unvollständige Migration V1→V2, neues WLAN, Teil-Reset.

  2. WLAN der Lampe neu einrichten (Pairing).

guides/gu10-led-flicker-dimmer-diagnosis.title: GU10/E27-LED flackert, Dimmer brummt, Nachleuchten — Diagnose
guides/gu10-led-flicker-dimmer-diagnosis.description: Systematische Diagnose: Flimmern am Dimmer, Brummen, Geisterlicht, Flackern bei 100 %. Schwierigkeit, Zeit, Kosten.
guides/gu10-led-flicker-dimmer-diagnosis.lead: Entscheidungsweg wie auf unserer französischen Seite. Bei Brandgeruch oder Verteiler: Elektriker rufen.
guides/gu10-led-flicker-dimmer-diagnosis.body:
1 — Main symptom

  • Flicker when on, especially at low dimmer setting → check dimmable marking, trailing vs leading edge, minimum load, replace incompatible dimmer.
  • Buzz from dimmer or lamp → halogen-era dimmer on LED, under-minimum load, mix of dimmable and non-dimmable — use LED-rated dimmer and matched bulbs.
  • Glow or flash when “off” → standby current through smart/no-neutral switch or dimmer leakage — bypass, compatible dimmable LED, or smart bulb with switch locked ON.
  • Flicker at 100 % on a simple switch → loose lamp, failing driver, or bad contact in GU10 holder — try another bulb, check lampholder.

Typical fixes (from our tree leaves)

Non-dimmable LED on dimmer → swap for dimmable or remove dimmer15–15 min£5–25
Leading-edge dimmer + dimmable LED → trailing-edge LED dimmer2–320–45 min£25–55
Single low-power LED below dimmer minimum → add load or “low load” dimmer2–325–50 min£10–50
Smart switch without neutral + ghosting → manufacturer bypass at rose3–430–90 min£4–15 parts (+ electrician)

Schritte

  2. If it was already installed: power cycle reset (off 5 s, on 5 s — repeat per Hue instructions for your model).

rooms/hallway.description: Flur in Zonen: Eingang, dunkler Abschnitt, Ecke, Boden. Tunnel-Effekt vermeiden.
rooms/hallway.lead: Flur in Zonen teilen — Eingang, gerader dunkler Abschnitt, Ecke, Boden — dann Kelvin, CRI und Dimmen abstimmen.
rooms/hallway.body:
Kurzfassung

  • Dark stretches: often 3500–4000 K plus several sources to avoid pools of shadow.
  • Corners: indirect wall light beats a single downlight.
  • Floor: discreet skirting or marker lights for night trips.
  • High CRI keeps door colours and paint true.

Long narrow hall — avoid the tunnel

  • Space luminaires along the length; large gaps create a “spot-spot” rhythm.
  • Downlight-only schemes leave walls dark — use wall washers or LED strip behind a cornice.
  • Low floor markers improve safety without glare.

Typische Fehler

  • One ceiling spot: loses the bend and casts facial shadow.
  • Too cool a white: feels flat and unwelcoming.
  • No dimming: cannot soften light at night.

Wo montieren

  • Outdoor wall lantern with bulb sheltered — luminaire at least IP44.

Trap: the sensor “sees” its own light

If the cell catches spill from the bulb, it may think it is day and cycle off/on. Point the sensor at open sky or use a fitting that shields it.

Drie cijfers onthouden

  • 420 lm per metre minimum: for a 3.0 × 0.6 m worktop, 500 lx × 1.8 m² × factor 1.4 (close source) ≈ 1,260 lm, i.e. 420 lm/m of cabinet run.
  • 4000 K and CRI (kleurweergave-index (CRI)) ≥ 80 (90 if you can) to judge food without a colour cast — see kleurtemperatuur and CRI.

Bar or LED strip?

A bar screws in and plugs in — about 15 minutes. Strip in an aluminium profile gives a continuous line but needs a sized 24 V driver. See under-cabinet LED strip.

guides/gu10-led-flicker-dimmer-diagnosis.body:
1 — Main symptom

  • Flicker when on, especially at low dimmer setting → check dimmable marking, trailing vs leading edge, minimum load, replace incompatible dimmer.
  • Buzz from dimmer or lamp → halogen-era dimmer on LED, under-minimum load, mix of dimmable and non-dimmable — use LED-rated dimmer and matched bulbs.
  • Glow or flash when “off” → standby current through smart/no-neutral switch or dimmer leakage — bypass, compatible dimmable LED, or smart bulb with switch locked ON.
  • Flicker at 100 % on a simple switch → loose lamp, failing driver, or bad contact in GU10 holder — try another bulb, check lampholder.

Leading-edge dimmer + dimmable LED → trailing-edge LED dimmer2–320–45 min£25–55

rooms/hallway.title: Gangverlichting: donkere hoeken, lumen, 3500–4000 K
rooms/hallway.description: Zones gang: entree, donker stuk, hoek, vloer.
rooms/hallway.lead: Gang in zones — entree, donker stuk, hoek, vloer — kelvin en CRI afstemmen.
rooms/hallway.body:
Quick summary

  • Dark stretches: often 3500–4000 K plus several sources to avoid pools of shadow.
  • Corners: indirect wall light beats a single downlight.
  • Floor: discreet skirting or marker lights for night trips.
  • High CRI keeps door colours and paint true.

Long narrow hall — avoid the tunnel

  • Space luminaires along the length; large gaps create a “spot-spot” rhythm.
  • Downlight-only schemes leave walls dark — use wall washers or LED strip behind a cornice.
  • Low floor markers improve safety without glare.

Common mistakes

  • One ceiling spot: loses the bend and casts facial shadow.
  • Too cool a white: feels flat and unwelcoming.
  • No dimming: cannot soften light at night.

Lux method: lumens and lux. Motion bulb idea: OSRAM radar E27 (3 m range limit). French detail: couloir page.

articles/dusk-to-dawn-bulb.title: Schemerlamp: fotocel vs. bewegingsmelder
articles/dusk-to-dawn-bulb.description: Fotocel brandt hele nacht. Buiten minimaal IP44.
articles/dusk-to-dawn-bulb.lead: Schakelt bij schemer in en ’s ochtends uit — ingebouwde fotocel.
articles/dusk-to-dawn-bulb.body:
Dusk-to-dawn vs motion sensor

Dusk-to-dawnMotion (PIR/radar)
On whenAll nightWhen someone passes
Best forPorch, façade lantern, “occupied” lookPath, garage, cellar
Energy~4–8 W × 12 h/nightVery low average
DeterrentConstant presenceSudden light

Where to install

  • Outdoor wall lantern with bulb sheltered — luminaire at least IP44.
  • Window lamp for holiday presence simulation.
  • Enclosed stair with no daylight: photocell may stay dark → bulb always on — wrong product.

Trap: the sensor “sees” its own light

If the cell catches spill from the bulb, it may think it is day and cycle off/on. Point the sensor at open sky or use a fitting that shields it.

Running cost (French regulated example)

5 W × 12 h/night ≈ 22 kWh/year. At the French regulated tariff 0.2001 € TTC/kWh (Base option from 1 August 2026 on the French market) that is about 4.40 €/year. UK: multiply kWh by your p/kWh unit rate.

Example product cited on FR site: Lucide ST64 filament dusk bulb 2200 K — Check price on Amazon UK. Solar alternative: Steinel XSolar.

Goals by zone

  • Table: flattering light, minimal shadow on faces — pendant sized to table width.
  • Sideboard: accent and easy search — strip or spots with CRI ≥ 90.
  • Mood: indirect, warmer in the evening, dimmable.

  • Single central pendant only — shadows on faces, table under-lit.

guides/error-code/govee-strip-overheatin.body:
Stappen

  1. Lower max brightness in Govee Home.
  2. Mount in an aluminium profile for heat spread.
  3. Do not exceed length per power supply rating.
  4. Unwind bundled loops that trap heat.
